To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in young survivors of MI the serum concentrations of LDL cholesterol and apo B, in combination with serum TG levels or VLDL TG levels, were the strongest discriminators between patients and controls, and the strongest correlates of the extent and severity (as estimated by the angiographic coronary artery disease scores) of CAD.

elevated levels of low-density lipoproteins (LDL) and apolipoprotiens B, but not other lipid or lipoprotein variables, are associated with the extent and severity, but not the number and severity, of coronary atherosclerotic lesions in young male survivors from myocardial infarctions.

the extent and severity, but not the number and severity, of coronary atheromas are related to the levels of serum lipids and apoproteins, whereas the severity of coronary lesions is related to the nonlipid risk factor, tobacco consumption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of serum lipids to coronary artery disease in young male survivors.

the study of the relationship of serum lipids and lipoproteins to angiographically determined diffuse coronary atheroma and stenoses in young male survivors (less than 45 years of age) of myocardial infarc-tion.
the relationship of serum lipids, lipoproteins or their apoproteins to coronary atherosclerosis in young survivors of acute myocardial infarct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in young male survivors with myocardial infarctions, the presence of coronary atheroma is strongly associated with elevated LDL cholesterol and LDL apolipoprotein levels.
lipoprotein abnormalities are associated with coronary atheromatous disease, but not with coronary atheroma.
the extent and severity but not the progression of coronary atherosclerosis in these young patients was related to serum lipid levels and apolipoprotiens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relationship of serum lipids and lipoproteins to coronary heart disease in patients under the age of forty-five is different from that observed in older patients.

the relationship of lipoprotein and nonlipid variables to coronary atheroma and stenoses in young survivors of MI is complex and that the extent of coronary atheroma is best related to the LDL cholesterol level.

in the young male survivors of MI, the extent of diffuse atherosclerosis was strongly related to the levels of serum lipoproteiin and apolipoprotien, whereas the number and severity or distinct stenosis were not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LDL cholesterol and apoproteins B are the most important factors that are associated with the development of coronary artery disease in young survivors of a myocardial infarct.
the LDL cholesterol and apoprotein B levels are strongly associated with the presence and severity of diffuse coronary atherosclerosis in young male survivors with myocardial infarctions.
LDL cholesterol is an important risk factor for coronary atheromatous disease, but that HDL cholesterol is not protective.
